# Forecasting an additional rating panel from old votes and four new votes

ChaosNLI collected 100 new ratings for disputed inference pairs from SNLI and MultiNLI. The previously examined five-vote archives include the earlier votes on overlapping items. This study uses fresh outcomes from a new rating panel. Fit each corpus separately. Normalize premises by case folding and collapsing whitespace, group all rows sharing a premise, and assign a group to test when the integer SHA-256 of its normalized premise modulo 5 is zero. All remaining groups are training. Remove groups with normalized premises shared between the two corpora. Retain every row with five valid old votes and exactly 100 new votes. Do not inspect new test distributions before fitting.

Target the probability of a fifth uniformly drawn new vote given all five old vote counts and four draws without replacement from the new panel. Integrate over every possible histogram of four new votes with its exact multivariate hypergeometric probability; score the cross entropy against the remaining 96. Each item has equal weight. No identities, texts, original construction label, or item IDs enter the forecaster. Test probabilities are scored under a without-replacement draw from one finite panel. No future raters were recruited.

Candidate is empirical Bayes on the exact empirical distribution of training panels given the old histogram. Mix a kernel over training items with matching old histograms with a uniform kernel over all training items (20 pseudo-items). The predictive rule weights each training panel by the probability of observing the four new votes there and forecasts its remaining 96 votes. Shrink the resulting table toward add-half new vote probabilities with equivalent sample size one four-vote context (effective cell count = training items x probability of context). This discrete prior can represent multimodality beyond a Dirichlet law. Inputs, sample and architecture fixed before seeing the panel results.

Comparators: new-only Jeffreys posterior mean; pooled old+new Jeffreys; new counts with a fitted Dirichlet-multinomial prior; the same prior fitted separately within each historical vote histogram with 20 pseudo-items pooled globally; and a saturated conditional table indexed by both old and visible new counts using all possible training panels, with context-dependent global backoff identical to the candidate. This positive control for reparameterization can exactly match a mixture of empirical panels. Report equivalence by algebra and maximum absolute paired prediction difference. Also fit an input-matched multinomial logistic regression predicting remaining votes from one-hot old histogram, one-hot new histogram and their cross, L2 penalty with C=1 and item weights from the hypergeometric distribution. Give every method the same split. A paper counts only for mean improvement of at least .005 nats and simultaneous positive 95% lower endpoints against every comparator in both corpora. Use a paired premise-cluster bootstrap with 5,000 draws and Bonferroni correction across the two corpora and six controls. If the saturated table matches the candidate, treat that as an identifiability result and stop this model line.
